2609.20484.title: Edustories: A Collection of Real-world Case Studies from Classroom Practices
2609.20484.paper_summary: Despite the widely recognized potential of AI in education, most prior work has focused on individualized student assistance. In contrast, the majority of educational practice worldwide still takes place in collective classroom settings. To enable researchers to study AI assistance in collective teaching, we introduce Edustories, a dataset of 1,492 teacher-written case studies describing real elementary and high-school classroom situations involving challenging student behavior, pedagogical interventions, and their outcomes. Among many other applications, Edustories enables evaluating LLMs' ability to predict the success of teacher interventions, crucial for providing practicing teachers with useful feedback. Comparing the latest models from four language-model families against expert assessments, we find that current models fall short of human expertise in predicting classroom outcomes; the strongest models reach 58% accuracy compared to 64% of human experts. This gap highlights both the limitations and the emerging potential of AI as assistants for practicing teachers.
2609.20484.paper_summary_zh: 儘管人工智慧在教育領域的潛力廣受認可，但大多數先前的研究仍然集中在個別學生的輔助上。相對而言，全球大多數的教育實踐仍然是在集體課堂環境中進行。為了使研究人員能夠研究集體教學中的人工智慧輔助，我們推出了 Edustories，一個包含 1,492 篇教師撰寫的案例研究的數據集，描述了涉及挑戰性學生行為、教學干預及其結果的真實小學和高中課堂情境。在許多其他應用中，Edustories 能夠評估大型語言模型（LLMs）預測教師干預成功的能力，這對於為在職教師提供有用的反饋至關重要。將來自四個語言模型家族的最新模型與專家評估進行比較，我們發現當前模型在預測課堂結果方面未能達到人類專家的水平；最強的模型達到 58% 的準確率，而人類專家的準確率為 64%。這一差距突顯了人工智慧作為在職教師助手的局限性和新興潛力。
